question: Pellow Grange say the unpaid service charge and insurance rent mean the break conditions aren't met. Is that what clause 9.2(a) actually says?
source: Lease - Unit 4 Merrow Arcade, Bath (24 June 2016)
evidence: (a) the Tenant has paid the Annual Rent due under this Lease up to the Break Date; and | for the avoidance of doubt references in this Lease to the Annual Rent are to the principal rent only and do not include the Service Charge, the Insurance Rent or any other sum reserved as rent by this Lease

also.source: Pellow Grange letter 17 October 2025 - break disputed
also.evidence: Clause 9.2(a) requires that, on the Break Date, the Tenant "has paid the Rents due under this Lease up to the Break Date".

also.source: Advice note - break clause, Unit 4 Merrow Arcade (LB draft)
also.evidence: Because the Lease makes the break conditional on payment of "the Rents", the unpaid service charge balancing charge and insurance rent must be paid before the Break Date or the break will fail.

also.source: Attendance note - client meeting 15 July 2025
also.evidence: cl 9.2(a) says Annual Rent only, not "the Rents"

note: No. The lease prevails: cl 9.2(a) requires only the Annual Rent, which cl 1.1 limits to principal rent, not the Service Charge or Insurance Rent. The DoV did not change (a). Pellow Grange misquote it as 'the Rents' and the LB draft repeats the error. The sums are still payable (pay pending dispute, interest), so paying under protest is sensible.

question: Lena's draft advice says we can still serve a fresh break notice at the Bristol address up to 24 December 2025. Is that right?
source: Deed of Variation - Unit 4 Merrow Arcade (15 October 2020)
evidence: 4.1 Clause 9.1 of the Lease is varied by deleting the words "six (6) months'" and substituting the words "nine (9) months'". | 4.3 For the avoidance of doubt, the Break Date remains 24 June 2026

also.source: Advice note - break clause, Unit 4 Merrow Arcade (LB draft)
also.evidence: Provided it is served on or before 24 December 2025 it will satisfy the six-month notice period in clause 9.1.

also.source: Attendance note - client meeting 15 July 2025
also.evidence: Lease says 6 mths BUT DoV 15.10.20 (Covid deal) changed it to 9 mths -> last day for service 24.9.25.

note: No. The draft uses the unamended six-month wording. The Deed of Variation (cl 4.1) made it nine months, so the last day to serve for the 24 June 2026 Break Date was 24 September 2025. A fresh notice now is too late, and 6 October 2025 receipt would also be out of time (the draft's 'eight months' point fails). The executed deed prevails over the draft note and SM's comment endorsing it.
